extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of public relations (PR educators, PR students, communications professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative dimensions drawn from a public relations textbook relevant to creating and assessing press releases, media relations, program planning, implementation, and evaluation. Covers objectives, messaging, media selection, presentation, legal/ethical constraints, and measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMART objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives should be SMART (specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound). (Referenced: SMART, 315)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears under Program objectives and Objectives — used for selecting and setting program objectives and for measuring program results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurable results
rubrics_metrics.description: Program results should be measurable. (Measurable results, 312–314)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linked to program evaluation and reporting; measurable outcomes are emphasized for interpreting and using results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program evaluation (levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program evaluation should be conducted at multiple levels and include qualitative and quantitative evaluation. (Program evaluation, levels of, 319–332; Qualitative evaluation, Quantitative evaluation, 324)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes summative impact assessments, unified evaluation model, and guidance on reporting and interpreting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretesting and program elements pretesting
rubrics_metrics.description: Program elements should be pretested prior to full implementation. (Program elements, pretesting, 277–279; Pretesting, 320)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pretesting is listed both as a program element and an activity to assess message and materials before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Use readability tests to assess the clarity/readability of messages and materials. (Readability tests, 321)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears under presentation quality / production values as a diagnostic for text aimed at target publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials should meet standards of presentation quality. (Presentation quality, 321–322)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linked to production values and readability; affects how media and publics perceive materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production values
rubrics_metrics.description: Production values of materials are an evaluative dimension. (Production values, 321)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider aesthetics, formatting, audio/visual quality for VNRs or press materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message content
rubrics_metrics.description: Message content must be crafted carefully. (Message, Message content, 170; 320)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears in chapters on message strategy, framing, dissemination and program planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message framing
rubrics_metrics.description: How a message is framed is a criterion (Message framing, 292–295).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing affects interpretation and persuasiveness; referenced in crisis and strategic messaging contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message placement / placement of program messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Placement of messages in media channels is an evaluative concern. (Message placement, 322–325; Placement of program messages, 322–325)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes channel selection, timing, and positioning to reach target publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message distribution / dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: How messages are distributed and disseminated is a dimension (Message dissemination, 300–301; Message distribution, 322).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers tactics for pushing content through earned, owned, and paid channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations guidelines / working with the media
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow guidelines for good media relations and working with media. (Working with the media; Guidelines for Good Media Relations; Press, working with, 230–232; Media relations, 209, 360)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes roles of the ‘person in the middle’, press conferences, press access, and international considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeliness of messages and responses is a criterion. (Timeliness, 293)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially important in news, crisis communications, and media pitching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty / oddity
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty or oddity in messages/materials can increase newsworthiness. (Novelty, Oddity, 293)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess potential to attract media attention and prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: Prominence influences media pickup and public attention. (Prominence, 84, 91, 174, 293, 324)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider celebrity, institutional prominence, or prominence of issue when evaluating coverage potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Repetition is a tactic for reinforcing messages. (Repetition, 309)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in planning to ensure message penetration and recall over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable / Scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Scheduling and timing of program implementation and media contact are evaluative factors. (Scheduling, 277)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes planning scenarios and calendar coordination with media cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target publics analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and analyze target publics (membership, position, psychographics). (Target publics, 267, 397; Membership of target publics, 270; Position of target publics, 270; Psychographics, 270)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drive message content, channel selection, and objectives; use stakeholder analysis and strategic publics concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct stakeholder or stakeholder-position analyses to inform strategy. (Stakeholder analysis, 246–248; SWOT, 248)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used during situation analysis and to define publics across situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation analysis / problem statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with a problem statement and situation analysis of internal and external factors. (Problem statement, Situation analysis, internal/external factors, 244–249)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms the basis for objectives, strategy, and research design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research methods: informal and formal
rubrics_metrics.description: Use listening and systematic research: informal methods (focus groups, key informants, social media listening) and formal methods (surveys, content analysis). (Listening as systematic research, Informal methods, Formal methods, 243–261)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research informs problem definition, planning, pretesting, and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and accountability of program implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor implementation and maintain accountability. (Monitoring of program implementation, 317; monitoring and accountability of, 317)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes program records, reporting, and adaptive management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting evaluation results
rubrics_metrics.description: Report evaluation findings clearly. (Reporting of evaluation results, 318; Program management, evaluation findings for, 318)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers what to report and how results should inform program utility and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified Evaluation Model
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply an integrated evaluation framework (Unified Evaluation Model, 319).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced as a structured approach to assess program impact and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program objectives: writing and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Write clear program objectives and select them via Management by Objectives and other processes. (Program objectives writing, 266, 271, 318; Management by objectives (MBO), 271)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives drive strategy, tactics, and evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program strategy: action and communication strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Design action and communication strategies; consider action before communication and action as open systems response. (Action and Communication Strategies; Action Before Communication; Action as an Open Systems Response, 273–275)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategy should integrate organizational actions with messaging for credibility and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive vs. reactive programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether programs are proactive or reactive and design accordingly. (Proactive programs, Reactive programs, 159–161)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects planning horizons, messaging urgency, and resource allocation; relevant in crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis communication checklist and crisis media strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a crisis communication checklist and specific media strategies for crisis situations (Crisis communication checklist, 283; Media strategy for Tylenol tampering crisis, 289).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses timeliness, transparency, message framing, and coordinated action during crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize transparency and engagement, particularly in public affairs and military public affairs contexts. (Transparency and engagement, 371–374)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linked to trust restoration and public acceptance; affects message credibility and legal/ethical risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional ethics and codes of ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to professional ethics, codes of ethics and the imperative of trust. (Professional ethics, Codes of Ethics, The Imperative of Trust, 116–121)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Influences decisions about truth, privacy, and acceptable persuasive tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal considerations: libel, privacy, copyright, trademark
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect legal constraints (libel, privacy, copyright, trademark, statutory law). (Reputation, Defamation and Privacy; Protecting PR materials: Copyright, Trademarks; Tort law (libel and privacy invasion), 139–143)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal issues shape message content, publication, and risk management in press materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media selection: traditional vs new media & channel characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose appropriate media channels (newspapers, radio, TV, cable, magazines, wire services, social media, SEO). (Traditional media; New media; Search engine optimization (SEO), 210–225, 221)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider media convergence, global transparency, audience reach, and channel affordances (e.g., YouTube, Twitter, social media channels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience/readership/viewership metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider readership, viewership, meters, share of voice and reach metrics (Readership, Viewership, Meter (television audience rating), Share of voice, 326–327, 324, 327).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audience measurement to evaluate placement effectiveness and media impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEO and online discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize digital materials for search engines and online distribution. (Search engine optimization (SEO), 221; Social media and Other Online Sources, 243–244)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant for press releases and online newsrooms to increase discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of broadcast tactics: VNRs and satellite media tours (SMTs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ broadcast-specific tactics such as Video News Releases and Satellite Media Tours. (Video news release (VNR), Satellite media tour (SMT), 7, 215, 220)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production values, timing, and media relations skills affect uptake by broadcast outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of factual accuracy and truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure truthfulness and avoid obfuscation/prevarication. (Truth, Obfuscation, Prevarication, 143, 308)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tightly linked to ethics, legal risk, and long-term reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program records and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain program records and documentation for accountability and evaluation. (Program records, 318)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports monitoring, reporting, and institutional learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare and train spokespersons and staff; technical communication skills and training materials matter. (Preparation, Training, Technical communication skills, 319, 279, 200)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects quality of media interactions, speeches, and crisis responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readiness of organizational policies and position papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Have policy documents, position papers, and backgrounders ready to support communications. (Policy Documents, Position Papers, Backgrounders, 199, 203–204)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for media queries, reputation defense, and informed messaging.
